transforms: none: the canonical languages/python/*.py are copied unchanged (message-ring and the -par variants excluded)

the stdlib is found from argv[0] (installs under /app/py-native and /app/py-wasm), so no PYTHONHOME/PYTHONPATH and no interpreter flags on any column; plain `python <script> <n>` shape as in the matrix
python3.13.wasm is precompiled once with wasmtime compile (default flags) to python3.13.cwasm and shared by all benchmarks; node runs the .wasm

PYTHONHASHSEED=0 on every column (the matrix does not pin it): with random seeds polymorphism splits into two modes 3.4% apart and the median of 5 lands in either; with seed 0 the native count is bit-identical run to run. Py_hash_t is 32-bit on wasm32, so the same seed still gives different hash values and dict layouts on wasm than natively; that difference belongs to the target
asymmetries: native-same-build and wasm are the same source, same LLVM 23.1.0, same configure options (--without-ensurepip --disable-test-modules --with-pymalloc --with-computed-gotos, default OPT -O3, no PGO/LTO/shared); remaining differences are the target itself
ILP32 vs LP64: SIZEOF_VOID_P/SIZEOF_LONG/SIZEOF_SIZE_T 4 vs 8 (sys.maxsize 2^31-1 vs 2^63-1); this is part of the wasm cost, not removable
libc: wasi-libc (dlmalloc, WASI emulated signal/getpid/process-clocks) vs glibc malloc for allocations pymalloc does not serve
pymalloc is OFF by default on WASI; forced ON for both builds. HAVE_MMAP is undefined on wasm, so pymalloc arenas come from malloc there and from mmap natively
threads: WASI builds use the stub thread layer (posix_threads=stub, no real GIL mutex/pthread); native uses pthreads
native module set is larger (zlib, bz2, ssl, sqlite... not used by the benchmarks); wasm links 69 builtin modules
reference column (matrix lang-lab-python) is the official gcc 12.2 PGO+LTO+--enable-shared build: not comparable as a wasm ratio, shown only for context
wasmtime gets the AOT .cwasm, node compiles the .wasm at start (cancelled by the differential)

stack: the wasm build keeps wasi-sdk's default 1 MiB linear-memory stack (no -z stack-size), native has the 8 MiB process stack; no benchmark recurses deep enough to reach either (tak and sort-search pass on both)

matrix.role: reference: the matrix image (official CPython build, gcc with PGO, LTO and --enable-shared), run with the matrix template; not a wasm control
